blogs.title: Start With the End in Mind: Lifetime TAVI Strategy When a Third Valve Might Be in the Cards
blogs.description: This post uses a TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV case to unpack lifetime management for aortic stenosis in the TAVI era. We’ll discuss first-valve choices that preserve future options (frame height, cell geometry, commissural alignment capability), how early CT planning can anticipate later valve-in-valve needs, and why coronary reaccess and effective orifice area must be budgeted from day one. We’ll highlight how platform selection and implant depth in 2014 and 2022 shaped what was feasible in 2024, and offer a practical framework for counseling patients about serial interventions.

blogs.title: Coronary Safety in TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV: Neo-skirts, Valve-to-Coronary Distance, and When to Forgo Protection
blogs.description: Coronary obstruction risk amplifies with each additional frame. We’ll walk through CT-driven assessment for serial valve-in-valve: coronary height, sinus of Valsalva and sinotubular junction dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance, and predicted neo-skirt height. The case illustrates a high implant to pin prior leaflets and keep the neo-skirt above the ostia, plus intraprocedural balloon testing with rapid pacing to confirm flow. We’ll contrast this strategy with BASILICA and chimney stenting—when to plan them, when to bail out, and when meticulous planning allows safe TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV without coronary protection.

blogs.title: Redo TAVI After Treated Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis: Navigating 2025 ESC Guidance and Real-World Trade-offs
blogs.description: Can you perform another TAVI after prosthetic valve endocarditis? We’ll synthesize the 2025 ESC stance (surgery preferred for PVE, but individualized decision-making) with a real-world path: documented infection control (targeted antibiotics, negative blood cultures), multimodality imaging to exclude active infection (TEE, CT), and prohibitive surgical risk with prior frames integrated into the aortic wall. We’ll outline patient selection, timing after therapy, the role (and limits) of suppressive antibiotics, and how to discuss uncertainty and recurrence risk with patients and heart teams.

blogs.title: Making Peace With Moderate Gradients: Interpreting Early Hemodynamics and PPM After Serial Valve-in-Valve
blogs.description: An immediate post-implant mean gradient of 67 mm Hg (DVI 0.24) fell to 27 mm Hg by one month and remained ~26 mm Hg at one year—what happened? We’ll dissect mechanisms behind early high gradients after serial TAVI: underexpansion that improves with post-dilatation and time, restoration of leaflet motion by mechanically expanding prior frames, and ventricular loading changes with early reverse remodeling. We’ll review how to interpret DVI, indexed AVA, and acceleration time after valve-in-valve, define prosthesis–patient mismatch thresholds, and set pragmatic expectations for what constitutes a “win” in triple-frame anatomy.

blogs.title: Why Acurate neo2 for the Third Round? Device Selection and High-Implant Technique in Triple-Frame Anatomy
blogs.description: Device choice matters more with each layer. We’ll explain why a supra-annular, relatively low-frame, alignment-friendly platform (Acurate neo2) was selected in a lumen narrowed to ~13.7 mm, and how preprocedural CT modeling informed leaflet-level alignment with the prior Evolut. Stepwise technique highlights include rapid-pacing balloon pre-dilation to test coronary safety, deliberate high implantation to pin old leaflets and minimize neo-skirt formation, and targeted post-dilation to optimize expansion without intentional frame fracture. We’ll discuss reproducible tips for commissural alignment across generations to maximize effective orifice area and preserve access.

blogs.title: Coronary Reaccess Through Triple Mesh: Practical Strategies for Tomorrow’s PCI After Today’s TAVI
blogs.description: After three frames, PCI can become an exercise in wire archaeology. This post focuses on preserving and executing future coronary access: pre-TAVI CT to map coronary “windows,” commissural alignment to avoid ostial overlap, and choosing frames with open-cell architecture and lower height when possible. We’ll cover fluoroscopic cues for alignment across platforms, how high implantation can keep reaccess corridors above the ostia, and practical PCI tactics (CT road-mapping, selective catheter shapes, guide extensions, microcatheters) when facing multilayered meshes.
